body:
Row-level deletes require a way to determine whether a given delete file applies to a data file.
The scope of a delete file will be limited in 2 ways: by time and by partition. Sequence numbers will be used to implement the first. All data and delete files will be added with a sequence number and deletes apply to any data file with a sequence number less than or equal to the delete's sequence number.
title: Add sequence numbers to metadata

body: One option for encoding row-level deletes is to track rows by file and row position in the file. This format should be documented in the spec.
title: Spec: Add file and position delete files

body:
One option for encoding row-level deletes is to track a tuple of values that indicate a row is deleted. The delete file will contain a subset of data columns and each row will be used to match data rows using equality.
For example, a delete file may contain a single 2: id column with 2 rows, 18 and 19. This indicates the any row with ID 18 or 19 is deleted in all files to which the delete is applied (limited by sequence number and partition scope).
This format should be documented in the spec.
title: Spec: Add column equality delete files

body: We have datasets which store milliseconds since epoch as a long column type. This column is currently being used for time-based partitioning. However Iceberg only supports time-based partitioning on timestamp and date column types with microsecond precision. Also, the transforms are all internal to Iceberg and not something that can be provided externally. How can we go about adding support for such a case in our environment? Do you think this is something that can be added to Iceberg itself?
title: Adding support for time-based partitioning on long column type

body:
The proposal is not about any logic change, but about code implementation.
In org.apache.iceberg.transforms.Dates and Timestamps, A private field called "name" is included as a String.
It seems that it is only used in toString() and could be substituted by ChronoUnit.toString() (although there are slight differences, like "year" (current name) vs. "Years" (ChronoUnit.YEARS.toString())
This change could make the code a little simpler, save some memory (by eliminating a field as String), and also be of the help when there is a need to add more constant into Dates and Timestamps enum, like SECOND... (is there any need ?)
title: Remove the private field of "name" from Dates and Timestamps
